title: Inhaled Hydrogen Therapy's Effect on Early Recurrences of Atrial Fibrillation Post-ablation.
official: Inhaled Hydrogen Therapy's Effect on Early Recurrences of Atrial Fibrillation Post-ablation. Phase II, Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled, Open-label Clinical Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to testing the perioperative inhaled hydrogen (H2) administration's effects during atrial fibrillation ablations (AF) to reduce both early and late recurrences associated with this procedure.

Researchers will compare H2 inhalation to the standard of care to see if we observe a reduction in AF recurrence after ablation but also a reduction in rehospitalizations or emergency visits for cardioversion, and consequently an improvement in quality of life.

Participants will:

* have an AF ablation associated to an hydrogen therapy or standard of care
* complete quality of life questionnaires
* record ECG on KardiaMobile©
* Keep a diary of their symptoms
* have a blood test
* have 2 follow-up visits (after 3 and 12 months) and 2 phone calls (after 6 and 9 months)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Be over 18 years old
2. Present with paroxysmal or persistent Atrial Fibrilation (AF) of less than 6 months with symptoms
3. Be a candidate for a first-time AF ablation (cryoablation and electroporation)
4. Understand and agree to comply with the study procedures
5. Patient must have a smartphone
6. Be enrolled in a social security scheme, or have equivalent rights
7. Have signed the study consent form

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Being over 80 years old
2. Having a left atrial diameter ≥ 50mm on transthoracic echocardiography
3. Radiofrequency ablation
4. Having a history of AF ablation
5. Patient on long-term anti-inflammatory treatment
6. Patient with gas administration equipment (CPAP, NIV…)
7. Woman of childbearing potential\*
8. Non-cooperative patient
9. In the exclusion period for another study
10. Persons covered by Articles L1121-5 to L1121-8 of the Public Health Code and Articles 31 to 35 of Regulation 536/2014 (corresponding to all protected persons: pregnant women, women in labor, breastfeeding mothers, persons deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision, persons receiving psychiatric care under Articles L. 3212-1 and L. 3213-1 who are not covered by the provisions of Article L. 1121-8, persons admitted to a healthcare or social facility for purposes other than research, minors, persons subject to legal protection measures or unable to give their consent).
11. Staff with a hierarchical relationship with the principal investigator
